shallot.ratio: Use 1/4 cup chopped yellow onion per shallot
shallot.note: Yellow onion provides a similar aromatic base, though slightly more pungent.

shallots.ratio: Use 1/4 cup chopped yellow onion per shallot
shallots.note: Yellow onion provides a similar aromatic base.

scallion.note: Green onions, chives, or finely diced yellow onion can substitute.

scallions.note: Green onions, chives, or finely diced yellow onion can substitute.

yellow onion.note: White, red onion, or shallots provide equivalent sweetness and moisture.

onion.note: Any allium onion can be used interchangeably.

garlic.ratio: Use 1/8 tsp garlic powder per clove of fresh garlic
garlic.note: Garlic powder provides the savory aroma when fresh cloves are unavailable.

butter.ratio: Use 3/4 cup olive oil for 1 cup butter in cooking
butter.note: Olive oil or vegetable oil works well for sauteing and sauces.

olive oil.note: Any neutral cooking oil can substitute.

breadcrumbs.note: Crushed crackers or panko breadcrumbs serve as an effective binder.

parmesan cheese.note: Pecorino Romano or Asiago offers similar salty, aged depth.

parmesan.note: Pecorino Romano or Asiago offers similar salty, aged depth.

dry pasta.note: Any shape of dried pasta can be swapped.

chicken broth.note: Vegetable broth or water with butter and herbs can substitute.

marinara sauce.note: Canned tomatoes or tomato sauce simmered with oregano and garlic.

ground beef.note: Ground turkey, chicken, or pork can substitute for ground beef.
